title: SLO-aware Variant Pricing Simulator — Product Playbook
author: Priya Narayanan
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the SLO-aware Variant Pricing Simulator (SVPS): a product component that models the cost and SLO impact of runtime variant selections (quantized vs full-fidelity, GPU family, session affinity) across tenant workloads. SVPS is intended for product, sales, and customer success teams to evaluate pricing proposals, show customers trade-offs, and drive rollout decisions for variant-based commercial packages.

Goals
- Provide simulated cost, latency, and quality outcomes for candidate variant policies before production rollout.
- Enable pricing experiments and what-if scenarios at tenant and portfolio level.
- Surface regressions in user-visible quality metrics tied to pricing changes.
- Produce reproducible scenario reports for commercial discussions and A/B experiments.

Scope and Non-scope
- In scope: modeling per-token unit costs, latency percentiles, KV-cache hit impacts, and fidelity-related quality deltas for variant routes. Includes a small scenario runner and a UI report generator.
- Out of scope: model training, model-level internal weight changes, or low-level kernel selection logic. SVPS consumes runtime telemetry and cost curves supplied by infra and Optimize service.

Key user personas
- Product Managers: evaluate commercial design choices and SLO guardrails.
- Sales / Solutions Engineers: generate customer-facing scenario comparisons during contracting.
- Customer Success: create migration plans for tenants moving between fidelity tiers.
- Platform Engineers: validate rollout policies against capacity and latency SLOs.

Success metrics (what success looks like)
- Accuracy targets: simulated p50/p90 latency within ±10% of measured after-rollout baseline for 80% of validation tenants.
- Business coverage: ability to simulate 95% of active hosted tenants’ traffic shapes using available telemetry inputs.
- Time-to-report: generate standard scenario report in < 90s for up to 1M simulated tokens.

Architecture summary
- Inputs: historical telemetry (token-level traces, route labels, KV cache hit rates), cost curves (per-device per-token cost), fidelity delta matrix (expected quality delta per variant), and tenant config (session shapes, routing policies).
- Core engine: event-driven simulator that replays sampled sessions, applies variant selectors, computes token-level latency and cost, and aggregates quality deltas.
- Outputs: per-route cost breakdown, latency percentile projections, end-to-end estimated revenue impact, and per-tenant risk scores.
- Integrations: Redwood-Optimize (cost curves), Console telemetry store (traces), Billing (for reconciliation), and Product UI (scenario builder).

Functional requirements (condensed table)
- Requirement ID: FR-001 | Title: Scenario builder | Description: UI and API to define tenant-level scenarios, including time window, variant mix, and traffic shaping | Owner: Product | Priority: P0
- Requirement ID: FR-002 | Title: Baseline ingestion | Description: Ingest last 30 days of telemetry for tenant and compute traffic archetypes | Owner: Eng-Platform | Priority: P0
- Requirement ID: FR-003 | Title: Variant policy simulation | Description: Apply candidate runtime policies and model cache/batching effects | Owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime | Priority: P0
- Requirement ID: FR-004 | Title: Report generation | Description: Export PDF/JSON reports with executive summary, tables, and recommended guardrails | Owner: Product | Priority: P1

Non-functional requirements
- NFR-001 (Performance): Scenario simulation latency ≤ 90s for datasets up to 1M tokens on standard SVPS cluster (4 vCPU, 16GiB).
- NFR-002 (Reproducibility): Every run must be seedable to produce identical outputs given identical inputs and seed.
- NFR-003 (Security): All tenant telemetry must be accessed with scope-limited service account and logged.

Simulation scenarios to support (examples)
1) Conservative migration: 20% of traffic to quantized variant during off-peak windows, monitor p95 latency and hallucination rate change.
2) Aggressive cost-slash: 50% prewarming + 40% quantized fallback; measure cost delta and customer-visible quality regressions.
3) Edge-optimized: route 30% of traffic to lower-memory variants in APAC region to test regional capacity-offload.

Quality and fidelity signals modeled
- Response similarity delta: BLEU/embedding-cosine shift per prompt-set (synthesized from tenant shadow-evals).
- Hallucination proxy: fraction of completions exceeding discriminator threshold from offline evaluator.
- Functional correctness: pass@k on tenant-owned eval prompt sets (when available).

Data model and inputs (short)
- Telemetry sample: route_id, timestamp, device_type, seq_len, tokens_generated, kv_cache_hit, latency_ms, tenant_id.
- Cost curve: device_type -> cost_per_token_usd (map).
- Variant metadata: variant_id, quant_level, expected_latency_factor, expected_quality_delta (per-prompt-set id).

API example (scenario submission)
Request (JSON payload sample):
{
  "tenant_id": "acct-12345",
  "window": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z/2026-10-07T00:00:00Z",
  "variant_mix": [{"variant_id": "v-q8-1", "pct": 30}, {"variant_id": "v-full-1", "pct": 70}],
  "seed": 20261123
}

Simulation outputs (fields)
- projected_cost_usd (string), projected_p50_ms, projected_p95_ms, estimated_quality_regression_pct, risk_score (0–100), recommended_safelock (boolean), scenario_id.

Telemetry & Dashboarding
- New Console page: SVPS → Scenario Library. Widgets: cost delta heatmap, latency percentile comparison, quality delta waterfall, and risk-by-route table.
- Alerts: auto-generate a high-risk alert when estimated_quality_regression_pct > 5% or risk_score > 70. Alert teams: product, ownership tag: eng-serving-runtime.

Pricing model mapping and guardrails
- Pricing inputs: per-token unit price, per-minute session surcharge, warm-capacity amortization.
- Guardrail examples: do not propose >40% quantized traffic for any SLO-backed tier; require canary at ≤5% initially.
- Commercial artifacts: SVPS report must include a recommended commercial credit buffer (USD) to be offered as migration protection.

Rollout plan (high-level)
1. MVP (Q4 2026): internal-only simulator with CLI and JSON reports; validate against 10 anchor tenants.
2. Beta (Q1 2027): Console scenario-builder + PDF report export; selected sales teams enabled.
3. GA (Q2 2027): Billing reconciliation hook and customer-facing UI; integration with purchase flow for variant addons.

Operational runbook (when simulation diverges from measured data)
1. Validate input freshness: check telemetry ingestion latency and sample size.
2. Re-run with smaller seed and different sampling method.
3. If discrepancy persists (>20% p95 mismatch): open incident and tag eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, and product for triage.

Ownership and stakeholders
- Product lead: Priya Narayanan
- Eng lead: Marco Silva (eng-serving-runtime)
- Data/Telemetry: Jonah Reed (eng-platform)
- Go-to-market liaison: Elena Park (sales-ops)

Release notes (first internal release)
- Feature: scenario builder CLI and replay engine.
- Known limitations: shadow-eval-based quality signals are approximate for unsupported languages; regional device cost curves are estimations.
- Migration notes: existing pricing experiments must have telemetry tags ("svps-enabled") injected to simulate historical runs.

Open questions and next steps
- How should SVPS account for cold-start GPU scheduling variance across Dedicated clusters? (action: capacity modeling spike task)
- Should the simulator expose per-prompt importance weighting for customers with skewed business-critical prompts?
- Decide default risk thresholds for commercial recommendations (proposal: risk_score 65 for enterprise review).

Appendix A — Example CLI commands
- Run a scenario locally (seeded): redwood svps run --tenant acct-12345 --window 2026-10-01:2026-10-07 --variant-mix v-q8-1:30,v-full-1:70 --seed 20261123 --out /tmp/report.json
